Subject: Annual renewal — scalable discount framework & sprint credits

Hi Lydia,

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a compact proposal on the table for Avery's renewal that balances predictability for you and capacity flexibility for spikes as you ramp into Q4. High-level outline below — happy to iterate.

Option A — 12-month committed capacity (recommended)
- 20% discount vs current pay-as-you-go unit rates for committed token volume (commits measured monthly).
- Seasonal "sprint credits": a pool of credits (10% of committed monthly units) you can use during product launches; unused credits do not roll forward but can be banked into a single quarter-level buffer once per year.
- Capacity safety-net: when monthly usage > committed + sprint credits, we cap incremental overage unit price at 150% of your committed unit rate for the first two overage months to avoid bill shock.

Option B — Retainer -> commit runway (9 months)
- Lower initial commit with right to escalate to full commit by month 9 with an applied pro-rata discount based on total 12-month consumption.
- Invoice smoothing via an escrow-style monthly reconciliation to reduce short-term cash volatility.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a quarterly usage export and a rolling 30-day lookahead to trigger sprint-credit recommendations.
- We can attach an SOW and a sample reconciliation worksheet; delivery timeline and SLAs unchanged.

If this looks directionally right, I can ask Ben to build a concrete pricing table with projected spend scenarios and a sample DocuSign addendum for procurement. Would you like us to include an invoice-escrow option for accounting to review?

Best,
Marissa
